summary: Kickoff scoping for POC benchmarking. Focus: translate Novum's client-side scripts into Redwood harness, decide streaming vs non-streaming for search+summarization workload, size workload partitions for multi-tenant tests, define success criteria (latency P95/99, cost per 1k tokens, failure rate), and align timelines for sample data, dedicated pool provisioning, and on-prem handshake.
transcript: 00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to run through the benchmark plan and how your client scripts will handshake with the harness. i think we have about 50 minutes so we'll leave time for questions. 00:18 Alex Werner: sounds good, quick context, Novum is running a product search + personalized snippet summarization flow. roughly 100k unique users/day, peak concurrency about 1.2k qps for search, and an async summarization fan-out that can hit bursts. 00:40 Diego Ramos: ok got it, and when you say summarization fan-out, is that synchronous in the request path or async background job? 00:48 Alex Werner: currently async background, but teams are debating moving part of it to sync for better UX — that's why we want to test streaming vs non-streaming for the summarization paths. 01:02 Priya Kapoor: high-level success criteria from Redwood's side: we want to help you hit latency targets while keeping token cost predictable. what's your initial SLA targets? 01:12 Samira Patel: P95 sub 250ms for search generation tokens, P90 sub 600ms for summarization when streaming, P99 under 1s for non-streaming summarization, and error rate under 0.2% sustained. 01:28 Maya Chen: great — makes sense. Diego, quick note: for the POC we propose two harness modes: client-script adapter (we run your scripts with small shim) and native streaming (we reproduce your streaming semantics inside the Redwood SDK). Decide both so we can compare end-to-end latencies. 01:46 Tom Hughes: question — how invasive is the shim? we have strict SRE policies and minimal package changes. 01:52 Diego Ramos: the shim is non-invasive, it's a thin wrapper that intercepts calls and forwards to the harness endpoint; we recommend you run it in a staging container as-is. there will be minor environment variables and a cert, nothing changes in the code logic. 02:06 Elliot Zhao: are there cases where the shim could change timing behavior vs native embedding? i.e., do we risk adding artificial latency? 02:12 Diego Ramos: minimal, but yes there's proxying overhead — that's why we recommend running both modes: 1) shim + your client scripts, 2) native SDK test to isolate infra latency. 02:24 Alex Werner: ok that works. next, workload partitioning: we have multitenant customers in a single cluster. we want to model three tenancy slices: small (80% traffic), medium (15%), enterprise (5%). can the harness drive that distribution? 02:38 Priya Kapoor: absolutely, the harness can weight traffic and simulate tenant ids, we can also replay KV cache warmups per tenant. 02:45 Samira Patel: KV cache warmups — pretty important. our live tail latency problems seem to correlate with cold KV cache on rare long histories. 02:56 Diego Ramos: note: our runtime does automatic prefix caching but for the POC we'll run experiments with cold/warm cache phases to measure cold start tail. we'll instrument KV cache hit ratio and cache size. 03:07 Tom Hughes: do you surface K V cash metrics in the console? 03:10 Maya Chen: yes, you'll get cache hit rates, per-route token counts, per-request latency, and token-level cost breakdown. 03:18 Elliot Zhao: for the benchmark scripts, we currently use a homegrown runner that emits streaming events every 50ms. is that compatible? 03:25 Diego Ramos: yes, but we need to standardize the streaming chunk sizes and the backpressure behavior. sometimes runners send tiny 1-char chunks which skew perf numbers — we recommend batchable chunk sizes ~128-512 bytes for realistic streams. 03:40 Alex Werner: ok we'll sanitize. Tom: any security blockers? 03:43 Tom Hughes: network egress policy: we cannot allow outbound traffic to public endpoints from our on-prem staging; is there an air-gapped option? 03:51 Priya Kapoor: Redwood Private supports VPC/on-prem connectors and air-gapped setups. for the POC we can provision a temporary private connector or do a short on-prem handshake where we deploy a relay in your staging that the harness talks to. 04:05 Samira Patel: what's the timeline to get a relay? 04:08 Maya Chen: typical network handshake and cert exchange is 5-7 business days. if you can provision a staging host and open the minimal ports we can do an initial smoke in 48-72 hours. 04:19 Elliot Zhao: cost modeling — we want cost per 1k tokens for the two modes. how precise is Redwood's cost reporting during a POC? 04:26 Diego Ramos: we provide token-level breakdowns and an estimated cost model using your vGPU profile; for Dedicated pools we attach actual vGPU runtime. during the POC we'll run a cost sim sheet. 04:36 Maya Chen: actionbacks: we'll include a cost projection sheet that maps throughput, quantization (int8 vs fp16), and streaming chunking to dollar per 1k tokens. 04:46 Alex Werner: excellent. another point: we need to run adversarial prompts as part of the benchmark to measure quality regressions when using quantized variants. can we plug in an eval set? 04:55 Priya Kapoor: yes, Redwood Optimize supports hooking evaluation sets to the benchmark run; we can run automated evals and surface score regressions alongside latency. 05:06 Samira Patel: perfect — our DS will send 2 eval sets: one for semantic quality, one for hallucination checks. 05:12 Diego Ramos: technical note: when we do streaming vs non-streaming, the harness will change tokenization thresholds and early stop behavior. we'll track alignment to your model outputs so quality comparisons are apples-to-apples. 05:24 Tom Hughes: regarding load shapes, peak qps is 1.2k but sustained is 300 qps. can you emulate diurnal spikes and booms? 05:32 Diego Ramos: yes, the harness supports Poisson, step, and sawtooth profiles, as well as trace replay from real telemetry. if you can share a production trace we can replay exact sequences including burst patterns. 05:45 Alex Werner: we'll share a 24-hour tcp-level trace sanitized. 05:48 Elliot Zhao: one sticking point is token budgets per request. our summarization sometimes truncates at 1k tokens which causes partial responses; we want to measure how different quantization modes affect truncation and latency. 05:59 Maya Chen: noted — include token budget variants in the load matrix. we'll put together a workload matrix with dimensions: tenant slice, streaming vs non-streaming, cold/warm cache, quantization mode, token budget. 06:15 Samira Patel: for success criteria, besides latency/cost/err_rate we want a runway metric: cold-start recovery time under x minutes and rollback thresholds if quality drops > 4% on eval. can that be automated? 06:27 Priya Kapoor: yes, our rollout policies can automate fallback to a safety model and trigger alerts. we'll wire that into the POC so you can see regression-based rollback events in the console. 06:40 Tom Hughes: onboarding docs—send the minimal dockerfile for shim and the environment variable list. 06:45 Diego Ramos: will do. also sending a troubleshooting playbook for common SSL / cert handshake errors. 06:52 Alex Werner: ok timeline recap? 06:54 Maya Chen: recap: Redwood to send benchmark plan and cost sheet by tomorrow (2026-04-16). Novum to upload client scripts and sample payloads by 2026-04-21. Redwood to provision temporary Dedicated / private relay estimate by 2026-04-20. Two-hour on-prem handshake scheduled w/c 2026-04-27 (TBD exact time). follow-up technical deep dive with Diego and Priya on 2026-04-22 to review load matrices. 07:18 Elliot Zhao: one more question, competitors — we evaluated Anthropic and RegionalCloudAI; our concern is model parity vs cost. can Redwood run a baseline against Anthropic Claudex? 07:28 Maya Chen: we can do a neutral baseline run, yes, but we'll need API keys and agreement on prompts. we'll include baseline as an optional experiment in the plan. 07:36 Samira Patel: great. that is all from our side. 07:40 Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll share notes and the plan. action items are in the chat and i'll follow up in CRM. 07:47 (meeting ends)
